Source: Kaspar.  24th March 1944.

Egon and Ursula LEHRBURGER.

Renewed enquiries have not merely completely confirmed my report of 27.2.44., but also provide the surest evidence that both LEHRBURGERS belonged to the Apparat of the Communist Party during their residence in Prague. This view is based on information from Gerda KRAUTTER, who was in personal contact with both LEHRBURGERS (and especially with Ursula) in Prague, also from Hans WISTUBA, of whom the same can be said, Maurice KEMPNER and Hans JAGER. It is confirmed also by DERKOW's enquiries in SOPADE and S.A.P. circles, as well as by Ernst HOLZER, who made exhaustive enquiries about the LEHRBURGERS some time ago and obtained information from a large number of persons.

Naturally not everyone of these people can confirm every detail of the report, but there is complete agreement in their fundamental verdict. It may be noted that they all stress the fact that Egon LEHRBURGER has always denied his membership of the party.

I also learnt from WISTUBA that while in Prague Egon LEHRBURGER denounced Erich WOLLENBERG as a Nazi. This WOLLENBERG was a demobilised officer of the last war who joined the German Communist Party, participated in the Eisner Putsch in Bavaria and was compelled to flee to Russia, where he became an officer in the Red Army, but subsequently quarrelled with the Party and was dismissed, after which he lived in the greatest penury in Moscow, where WISTUBA met him in 1932. Fearing that his personal liberty was in danger he risked an effort to leave Russia with an illegal Swiss passport he had used for former Apparat activities, and succeeded in getting through to Czechoslovakia. The German Communists there, who naturally knew that he had fallen into disgrace in Moscow, put every possible obstacle in his way, and eventually LEHRBURGER denounced him to the Prague police as a dangerous individual and a Nazi suspect. He got wind of this through a personal friend and fled to France to avoid impending arrest. He was in touch with RETZLAW in Paris until shortly before the German occupation, when he fled with him to Marseilles, where for some reason they got separated, so that RETZLAW came over here alone, while WOLLENBERG ended up in North Africa, where he is at present. He is still in correspondence with RETZLAW.
